messages:
maria-g: heads up — console heatmap shows p95 jump for /v1/embeddings after we shifted rollout weights to new variant. client traces and gateway logs don't match the same magnitude. anyone seeing split in telemetry?
kevin: I can see a bit of a bump in server-side aggregates. do we know if this is coming from a route fanout change or a quota fallback?
samir: @maria-g can you paste the console slice you looked at? p95 can be sensitive to low-sample cohorts.
maria-g: screenshot pasted in thread (omitted here). sample counts look ok for the main cohort, p50 is flat but p95/p99 moved. interestingly the endpoint-level breakdown on the new variant shows higher dispatch latency but infra traces look normal.
jia: could be that the new variant has different tokenization cost distribution (longer sequences) which only shows up in tail percentiles. did we compare sequence-length histograms?
lucas: also check if any requests got routed through the reserve capacity pool — that can inflate tail if it queues. routing logs show a small % routed to reserve at 09:42.
kevin: adding to that — our console rollup uses tdigest merge with a slightly different compression than the raw traces. small shifts in chunking+merge can move p95 surprisingly. I flagged an issue earlier: tdigest compression param mismatch between ingest and rollup.
maria-g: hmm. so three hypotheses: sequence-length skew, reserve pool fanout, tdigest merge artifact. which is quickest to validate?
samir: quick validation plan: 1) run a raw-sample query for that endpoint for the timeframe (no rollup) 2) diff sequence-length percentiles 3) check route-tag on routed requests. Something like:
```
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) AS p95, count() AS n FROM raw_spans WHERE endpoint = '/v1/embeddings' AND ts BETWEEN 1710000000 AND 1710003600 GROUP BY sequence_bucket
```
kevin: I'll run the raw_spans query and dump sequence_bucket counts. pinging @deploy-bot to surface any reserve-pool activations around that time.
deploy-bot: reserve-pool activation: variant-burst-reserve engaged at 2024-04-12T09:41:58Z for 64s (triggered by quota-threshold).
jia: that timing aligns. if reserve pool queued for 60s, you'd expect tail skew without backend CPU changes.
lucas: low-effort mitigation: for rollouts we should mark the reserve pool in console slices and annotate the timeline so SREs see fallback windows.
maria-g: Agreed. Can we also surface merge-config in the percentile lineage UI? It's really hard to correlate when rollup compression differs from raw.
kevin: +1. I'll open a follow-up RFC for pct lineage metadata (ingest compression param, whether tdigest or histogram, sample counts).
samir: also a short-term dashboard note: add a toggle to overlay raw-sample p95 vs rollup p95 for critical endpoints. helps detect merge artifacts quickly.
maria-g: thanks all. action items: kevin runs raw queries and posts snippets; kevin opens RFC for lineage metadata; lucas/ops to annotate reserve-pool events in console timeline; samir to prototype overlay toggle.
kevin: posting raw sample p95: p95_raw=312ms, p95_rollup=450ms, sample_count_raw=2380. sharing query results in #eng-platform-dumps.
maria-g: that's pretty conclusive that merge/compression is amplifying tail. will hold the rollout until we have lineage visibility + reserve annotation. :white_check_mark:
